value.rationale: Reliability at late times is determined by the exponential survival rate, not the expectation. The sharp inverse-square near-reset scaling c/L^2 creates a natural balance between near-site rarity and far-site travel, producing a nontrivial first-order selection boundary c*, a macroscopic change in best physical reset rate, and the explicit finite-size shift K. The complete asymptotic optimization resolves a structural gap in a published physical model, not an arbitrary fixed-parameter computation.
